# PR 400 Branch Code Review and Clarifying Comments

## Requirements

- Review all code changes relative to the branch merge base with `origin/main`,
  including the current uncommitted private backend planner.
- Add brief clarifying comments where assumptions, critical decisions or
  non-obvious invariants warrant explanation. Do not narrate obvious code.
- Report substantive correctness or behavioral issues separately; comments must
  not conceal bugs or imply unimplemented Azure behavior exists.
- Preserve existing behavior and repository conventions.

- "review all code changes in this PR branch and always add clarifying but brief

## Decisions

- Use the resolved default branch `origin/main`, not a guessed branch.
- Include working-tree changes so the latest provider slice is not omitted.
- Review generated output for consistency; put explanations in handwritten
  sources rather than manually editing generated code/schema.
- Preserve the existing implementation; report unrelated or behavioral defects
  for a separately approved repair.
- Explicit approval received before making this task's source-code changes.

## Implementation Details

- Initial inventory: 55 committed changed files, plus uncommitted backend planner
  and Gateway integration. Documentation supplies context; source and test changes
  are the primary review scope.
- Source edits for this review are comments only; no executable behavior changed.
- Reviewed the API/deep-copy/schema changes; annotation parser and tests;
  both changed manager entrypoints/tests; object metadata constants; Gateway,
  GatewayClass, model, resolver/index and HTTPRoute packages with their tests;
  member discovery/export changes/tests; the new backend planner/tests; Makefile,
  member chart conditions, E2E suite/helpers and bootstrap additions.
- Compared the resolver's port/conflict checks with the existing hub export
  controller and condition-generation helpers. Their strict snapshot/port
  equality is intentional, not a new order-insensitive comparison contract.
- Comments will clarify the verified internal-frontend trust boundary, shared
  discovery deadline, stale-metadata withdrawal, independent feature flags,
  generation-aware status ownership, authorization-before-target-reads, zero
  member weights, normalization versus routing precedence and backend naming.

### Review findings and boundaries

- No new high-confidence behavioral defect identified in the implemented subset.
- Existing release blockers remain: complete routing/domain lowering and API
  verification, Azure ownership/provisioning/observation/deletion, Gateway-manager
  deployment packaging and real integration/private-traffic evidence.
- The scale document incorrectly says no Gateway reconcilers are registered.
  Correct its status and diagram narrowly; retain provisional limits and
  unimplemented Azure/generated-route capacity gates.
- The Gateway E2E suite exercises API round trips, not actual attachment/grant
  enforcement, private-origin discovery or AFD traffic. Its synthetic exports are
  unsuitable as valid private-ingress fixtures; clarify rather than imply proof.
